t: The religion centred on sacrifices and fire rituals recorded in the Vedas, among them the Agnihotra, the Soma rituals and the Ashvamedha, the horse sacrifice, offered to deities such as Indra, Agni and Varuna.
Ancestor worship was an important, perhaps the central, part of the early religion, which mentions an afterlife but not the later doctrines of karma and reincarnation.
In the late Vedic period it developed into Brahmanism, which gave great weight to the priestly Brahmin class and helped to shape contemporary Hinduism, though the two differ significantly.
dyk: The oldest inscriptions in Old Indic, the language of the Rig Veda, were found in northern Syria, where the Mitanni kings took Old Indic throne names and used the term ṛta, meaning cosmic order and truth.
ev: The early Vedic period begins, when the religion is found in the western Ganges plain
The late Vedic period begins, as Indo-Aryan people move into the Gangetic Plain and become settled farmers
Brahmanism takes shape in the Ganges basin
The Brihadaranyaka Upanishad discusses the earliest versions of the karma doctrine
The Vedic period is held to end
The earliest recorded manuscript of the Vedas, found in Nepal, is written

f.origin: the northwest Indian subcontinent (Punjab and the western Ganges plain), in the early Vedic period from c. 1500 BCE, with roots in the Indo-Iranian religion of the Sintashta and Andronovo cultures
f.founder: none: it grew out of Indo-Iranian religion and the Bactria–Margiana culture, then took shape in the northwest of the subcontinent
f.scriptures: the Vedas, the four Samhitas with the Brahmanas, Aranyakas and some of the older Upanishads, composed in Vedic Sanskrit and first handed down by oral transmission
f.followers: none as a religion of its own after the Vedic period, which is held to have ended around 500 BCE; it became Brahmanism and then Hinduism, and some Vedic rituals are still practised today
